title: The Man Who Didn't Eat for 382 Days
sources: Survival 'rule of threes' (about 3 minutes without air, 3 days without water, 3 weeks without food) is a common rough guideline; actual limits vary widely with conditions (e.g. Wilderness Medical Society guidance; Piper 2014 overview)

Angus Barbieri, a 27-year-old from Tayport, Scotland, fasted for 382 days (June 1965 – July 1966) under medical supervision at Maryhill Hospital, Glasgow, taking only water, tea, coffee, soda water and vitamin/mineral supplements; his weight fell from 456 lb (207 kg) to 180 lb (82 kg), a loss of about 125 kg (Stewart & Fleming 1973, Postgraduate Medical Journal 49:203–209; Guinness World Records)

lines.text: You can survive three minutes without air.
And about three weeks without food.
In nineteen sixty five, a man in Scotland went three hundred and eighty two days without eating.

lines.text: Doctors watched him the whole time. He only had water, tea, and vitamins.
